issues.description: In the template repository the Bitmap24 class header declares a method named write(const std::string&), but the implementation file and the rest of the code (main.cpp) call/define save(const std::string&). The solution repository consistently uses save(...). This name mismatch in the template (header vs. implementation and usage) will cause build failures or confusion for students trying to compile and run the example program.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template header and implementation consistent with the rest of the code and the solution. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from write(const std::string&) to save(const std::string&), or alternatively rename the implementation and all usages to write(...). The simplest fix: update the template header to declare void save(const std::string &i_filename); to match Bitmap24.cpp and main.cpp.

issues.description: The Bitmap storage method is named inconsistently in the template: the header declares Bitmap24::write(const std::string&), while the implementation defines Bitmap24::save(const std::string&). The solution repository consistently uses save(...). This mismatch in the template creates a direct mapping and build problem (students see a declared API 'write' but the implementation provides 'save'), causing confusion and potential linker errors rather than a simple naming preference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the solution: change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'void write(const std::string &i_filename);' to 'void save(const std::string &i_filename);' (or alternatively rename the implementation to 'write'), so header and implementation match and align with the solution's API.
